scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the user did something wrong by giving his girlfriend cooking tips. Let me break this down step by step.

First, the user and his girlfriend have been together for a while, and they moved in together six months ago. They agreed that she would handle cooking because she gets home earlier. That makes sense because she can start cooking while he's still at work, so he comes home to a hot meal. But the issue is that her cooking isn't up to his standards. He says she's not terrible, but it's far from what he was used to. So, he started giving her pointers to help her improve.

He mentions that he always ate everything and said thank you, so he wasn't being rude. He thought he was just being helpful. But then, when his mom visited, he suggested that his mom could give his girlfriend some cooking advice. His girlfriend seemed fine at the time, but after his mom left, she got really upset, accusing him of humiliating her in front of his family. She went on a cooking strike, refusing to make anything for him.

The user thinks she's overreacting because he never complained or threw out her food. He just wanted to help. Now he's wondering if he did something wrong or if his girlfriend is being unreasonable.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for him to give her constructive criticism about her cooking, especially in front of his mom?

I need to consider a few things here. First, the intention behind his actions. He says he wanted to help her improve, which is a good intention. But the way he delivered the criticism might have been the issue. Even though he wasn't rude, offering advice in front of his mom could have made her feel judged or embarrassed, especially since she's not confident in her cooking skills.

Another point is the agreement they had. They both agreed that she would handle cooking, so he shouldn't have expected her to be a perfect cook. It's one thing to offer help privately, but doing it in front of family might have crossed a line.

Also, his girlfriend's reaction seems intense, but it's possible that she felt unsupported and undermined. When he suggested his mom could help, it might have felt like he was implying she wasn't good enough, even if that wasn't his intention.

So, while his intention was good, the way he delivered the criticism and the context in which he did it might have been insensitive. Therefore, his action might not be entirely morally acceptable because it caused harm to their relationship, even if unintentionally.
